utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case, as soon as the accused enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They're here. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This is case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor against Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and to everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Tecla Henry-Benjamin, Daryl Mundis, and we're assisted today by our intern Jaspreet Saini, and our case manager, Andres Vatter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. The Defence teams appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel, Stefane Bourgon, co-counsel, and Muriel Cauvin, legal assistant. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura today, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On Tuesday, 7 December, the Chamber would like to greet everybody, the Prosecution, the Defence teams, the accused, as well as all the staff present in this courtroom. Today we shall continue the hearing of the witness that we started yesterday, but the Defence, before that, wanted to make a few remarks. That's why I'm going to give them the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would just briefly like to address Your Honours with regard to the testimony of our witness Mr. Mirsad Mesic. He is supposed to appear on -- he appeared on Friday. During the testimony of this witness, the Trial Chamber put several questions to the witness, and I would like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to a fact in that regard. During his testimony, Witness Mesic also spoke about the testimonies heard before. I would like to say that, with regard to the witnesses that he mentioned during his testimony, there were certain problems with regard to a possible -- their possible -- a possible suspicion of their credibility. I would just like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber that some questions that went to the credibility of these witnesses were already put before. On the 20th of May, 2004, during the testimony of Witness ZO, during the cross-examination of this witness, which is recorded in the transcript on 20 May, on pages 7777 through to page 7780, a few issues were raised that might go towards the credibility of these witnesses. I'm mentioning this because the Defence is trying to bring before this Trial Chamber only credible witnesses. All of us in the courtroom, obviously, reserve the right to put questions that go to their credibility; however, we are very clear, Your Honours, that the testimony of every witness will be heard according to the Rules and regulations, and will be evaluated by the Trial Chamber according to the Rules and regulations. And we don't have any reservations or doubts about that. However, we would like to tell you that so far we have expected that, and I believe that the Trial Chamber has enabled us to -- for every one of our witnesses to be heard, in keeping with Rule 21, and for every witness not to be more or less -- have more or less credibility than any of the witnesses brought before this Trial Chamber by the Prosecution. I believe that you will appreciate that the Defence is in a very difficult situation. None of the witnesses find it easy to appear before this Trial Chamber. Please bear that in mind. This was why we had decided to address you particularly with regard to this witness. Thank you for having heard this Defence team, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give the floor to Mr. Mundis. But if I understand well the position of the Defence, the Defence has indicated to the Trial Chamber that there were questions put to the witness which went towards his credibility, and that with regard to these questions, the witness -- the Defence has told us that the witnesses that come as Defence witnesses are credible at least to the extent that the Prosecution witnesses were credible. I believe that this is what the Defence has stated in their address.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you have understood well that every witness that we bring is credible. However, this particular witness doubted the credibility of the other two witnesses, and this is what I wanted to -- the Trial Chamber to be aware of. This was not the first witness that questioned the credibility of these two witnesses. These two witnesses' credibility was already tested on the 20th of May, and this is recorded in the transcript on the pages that I have mentioned a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution at this point will just make two very brief comments, the first being that we have no doubts about the intention of either Defence teams with respect to calling witnesses that they believe will be credible. Of course, one of the primary purposes of both cross-examination and, in certain circumstances, questions put to the witness by the Trial Chamber within the scope of its latitude in examining witnesses can go to the credibility of a witness. The primary reason why I rose to my feet, though, Mr. President, is to put forward our position that the proper time for arguing the credibility of specific witnesses is not at this point of trial. These type of arguments are best served, in our humble submission, at the end of the trial, after all the evidence has been heard. And for that reason, the Prosecution position is that it's improper for any of the parties to be commenting on or arguing about or cross-referencing witness testimony at this stage of the proceedings. There's a time for that, and that is during closing arguments, once all the evidence is in. And our respectful view, Mr. President, is that it's inappropriate at this time to be making the types of comments that my learned colleague has made, and it is, in fact, a form of argumentation which, in our submission, is best left for the end of the trial, once all of the evidence is in. And Your Honours will then be able to assess the credibility of individual witnesses in light of the entirety of the testimony. In that respect, the parties will be able to fully brief and argue the credibility of all the witnesses and, in fact, all of the evidence which is placed before Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give the floor to Mr. Bourgon in a couple of minutes. But if I understand the position of the Prosecution well, they say that, as regards the credibility of the witnesses, it is going to be at the end of this trial that the Trial Chamber will be able to assess the credibility of the witnesses. So all the elements have to be integrated, and it would be premature at this stage to say or think or speculate about the credibility of any one witness. The witnesses have to be assessed within the entirety that arises from all the testimonies of all the evidence, and that is only going to be possible at the end. I don't think that there are any particular problems in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would just like to provide a clarification. Perhaps my colleague didn't understand the objective of our arguments, our submissions, this Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond afternoon. We're not arguing about the credibility of such a witness; that's not our objective. We simply want to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to the following fact, and we want this to be included in the transcript: The witness who testified last Friday was not the first witness to draw the Chamber's attention to the issue of the credibility of the two Prosecution witnesses. That's the only comment we want to make. We're not saying whether these witnesses are credible or not. But what we believe is that it is important that the Chamber take note of the fact that this isn't the first witness who has put into question the credibility of these two witnesses. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have taken note of what you have just said. As far as the issue of credibility is concerned, I would personally say that the term "credibility" contains a number of conceptions within it. There can be a witness who is credible and who is a witness in good faith. He believes that an event took place in a certain manner, although that might not be the case, so one might consider such a witness to be a witness on the basis of what the witness says. But there's also the issue of credibility which is affected when the truth isn't actually what the witness has said, and this is a different issue. So this is a very broad concept which can cover a number of situations. And naturally, it's for the Judges to assess these situations but, naturally, in light of all the evidence presented. And as you have said, because a witness mentioned something on Friday that contradicts what other witnesses said, this doesn't mean that certain conclusions should be drawn, even though someone's testimony was contradicted by several other witnesses. It's only at the end that we will see these issues clearly. I think everyone agrees, but it was necessary to emphasise this issue. Thank you for the submissions that both the parties have made. We'll now call the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, General. I hope you had a good evening, a good night, that you're rested. As you know, we shall be working until 7.00 this afternoon. Tomorrow you will be free; there will be no hearings on account of the Plenary Session of the Judges. So we will invite you, after this evening, to come back on Thursday. If you hear the interpretation of my words, I'm going to give the floor to the Defence who are going to proceed with their examination-in-chief. I believe that you will base your examination-in-chief on the binders that you provided us with yesterday, unless there are some new binders. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Residovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, let me just adjust the -- my headphones. Mr. President, it is correct that before I start putting my questions to the witness, I would kindly ask the usher to give you the other set of documents that we adjusted according to your suggestions. In order to facilitate the work of all of us in the courtroom, we adjusted our documents. We managed to do that for the witness, for the Trial Chamber, and for myself, as I will be putting the questions to the witness. I apologise to my learned friends, who will still have to make an effort to find the document that I will be referring to during my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we have a binder with tabs. This is very good. I hope that Mr. Mundis has the same binder, with the same tabs? If not, I'm prepared to offer you my binder, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It appears as though I've received a stack, Mr. President. We'll try to make due. If my learned colleague is proceeding too quickly, I'll just have to ask her to slow down. We'll do the best we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, yesterday, at the end of our day, we started talking about the political goals of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna that you were aware of. And we also were talking about behaviour of the HVO in the course of 1992, and you told us about some of your personal experiences and knowledge arising from your relationship with the HVO in the course of 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you, General, to refer to the binder and look at documents number 1, 2, and 3. Document number 1, under tab A, bears the Defence number 0366; number 2 is Defence number 0369; and number 3 bears the Defence number 0381. The first document is a document that originates from the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The date is 21st July 1991. I would kindly ask you, General, to look at the last page of this document in B/C/S, and read paragraphs 2, item 16 and item 17. These paragraphs speak about the recommendation to the Croatian population of the Travnik region and Herzegovinian municipalities to join the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And then look at number 18, which speaks about the initiative launched in the Travnik region to establish the Croatian National Council of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Have you been able to look at these two paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the second document, which is also a document that originates from the Croatian Democratic Union of the Herzegovinian region, and represents conclusions from a joint meeting which was held on 12 November 1991, I would like to draw your attention to the first paragraph in which in the conclusions, people are invited to accept conclusions adopted at meetings with Franjo Tudjman on the 13th and 20th June 1991, in Zagreb. These two regional communities, starting from the conclusions and meetings in Zagreb, through special conclusions that were reached in Grude, and then on the 22nd of October in Busovaca, and on this day, on 12 November 1991, unanimously and jointly decide that the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina have to finally engage in a decisive and active politics that would lead to the realisation of our long dream to have a joint Croatian state. In the next paragraph - can you see it - there is mention of the proclamation of the Croatian banovina name in Herzegovina. Under item 2, it is pointed to the existing forces which opposed the historical interests of the Croatian people, and here Bosnia and Herzegovina is proclaimed in the second sentence, saying these forces are advocating the non-existing sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina. And later on, in the last sentence of this paragraph, it says: "We have to show Europe and the world what are the Croatian areas in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and where we're going to build our future."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm wondering if there's a question anywhere in the past couple of pages. But I'd also note for the Chamber that the three documents which my learned colleague has now drawn the witness' attention to do not appear on the list of documents dated the 29th of November, 2004, which were likely to be shown to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the second question is concerned, we have already explained that we could not provide this last week, and we could not put it on the list of our documents. However, we provided our colleagues with the entire list on the 3rd, showing all the documents that we were going to show to the witness. And these documents are on our additional list. My question, and now I'm referring to the first part of the Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis posed the same problem yesterday. Prosecution, did you get the documents on the 3rd of December that were provided to the Registry? I've had these documents. Do you have all these documents that were provided to you on the 3rd of December? Yesterday you already raised this problem, and the Defence has told us that these documents are among the documents that were provided to you on the 3rd of December. There is a list that was provided to you on the 3rd of December. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I have not seen a list dated the 3rd of December that specifically relates to this witness. We have over the weekend and yesterday a large number of additional documents that relate to the exhibit list of the witness. But I am unaware of any specific list of documents to be used with this witness after the 29th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the Defence has explained that before the 29th of November, they made an additional list. The date of this list is the 3rd of December, and it was registered with the Registry on the 3rd of December. According to the Defence, the documents that you have just mentioned are on that list. Maybe the Prosecution should refer to the list that they got on the 3rd of December and see what the new documents are. So what about the first part of the question? You wanted to enumerate the paragraphs that are going to be mentioned in the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have just reminded the witness what he told us yesterday about, about the political goals of the Croatian Community of Bosnia-Herzegovina which wanted to separate parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina from the state. And now I'm showing the witness three documents, and I'm asking him to tell me whether these documents actually confirm what he himself told us yesterday without having the opportunity to refer to these documents. This is my only question arising from these documents that I'm putting to this witness now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot say whether I've ever had the opportunity to see these documents, because when I testified before, before this Tribunal, I was shown a number of documents originating from the Croatian Defence Council and the Croatian Democratic Union. But I can be sure of one thing, and that is that in 1991, in 1992, 1993, as well as 1994, I did not have an opportunity to see these documents. Your Honours, yesterday I was testifying about the things that I experienced during that time. At that time I was not aware of these documents. I didn't see them; I was not aware of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, were you aware of this politics being implemented, the politics that is mentioned in these documents? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I could see that they were trying to implement the policies adopted by the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at the following documents: Documents under section B; number 1, DH36; number 2, 0396; number 3, DH35/ID; number 4, DH410; number 5, 412; number 6, 413; number 7, 417. And if you can have a look at them, could you first tell me whether these documents reflect the situation you mentioned yesterday; namely, that the HVO had declared the BH army illegitimate, it introduced Croatian currency, and it was trying to establish parallel bodies of power. And document 0396, is this document, in fact, an order on the basis of which you yourself were arrested and maltreated?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I, in fact, experienced during this period of time, and I mentioned this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, yesterday you also spoke about the establishment of parallel organs of power. Could you please have a look at document DH453, under number 9; and then have a look at DH0459, document number 0459, under number 10; under number 11, have a look at document 464; document 12, 474, which you signed yourself; under number 13, document 485; and have a look at number 14, DH489. Do these documents reflect what you testified about yesterday; namely, that in 1992 you experienced a number of incidents, you were prohibited from passing through, you were controlled, weapons of the Territorial Defence were taken away, the legitimate organs of power were disbanded, as stated in the announcement for the public, under number 13. And as said in document 0474, did you inform your superior command of all these events, and did you inform them of the immense problems that you had to confront in the field? Do these documents that, in fact, confirm what you testified about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All these documents confirm what I was saying yesterday. Yesterday I provided you some specific examples, and these documents show that that is, in fact, what happened in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, yesterday you also said that General Hadzihasanovic's task to gather forces and set off towards Sarajevo wasn't a task he could carry out immediately; this task had to be postponed. After the corps was formed, did the 3rd Corps do what it could in order to prepare some of the forces to make another attempt at lifting the blockade of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said the first attempt to gather the necessary number of troops to lift the blockade of Sarajevo failed. But in the regional staff, and in the 3rd Corps, and especially after the establishment of the 3rd Corps, we didn't abandon the task to gather forces that could be used to lift the blockade of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do you remember, or do you know whether at the time the 3rd Corps also suggested to the HVO that, as an armed force, it should participate in the fight to lift the blockade of Sarajevo, that they were an armed force fighting this aggressor. Do you know what their attitude was?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that the 3rd Corps command, in December 1992, forwarded an official letter to the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and it requested that they participate with units of the Territorial Defence in lifting the blockade of Sarajevo. After a short period of time, we received a reply stating that the HVO units were not in a position at that time to participate in lifting the blockade of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you please have a look at the following documents: Document number 7, DH224/ID; then document number 8, 0537; and document number 9, 0536.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are those documents under section C?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what you said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Documents number 7, 8, and 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as document 7 is concerned, we don't have the translation into English, or at least I don't have the translation of this document. It's document 417; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is under section C; section C, document number 7, and the number is DH224/ID. Unfortunately there is no translation of document number 8, whereas document number 9 has been translated. I would first like to ask the General to answer my question that concerns the first document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a document from the 3rd Corps in which they requested that the HVO participate in lifting the blockade of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can recognise this document. It's a document drafted by the 3rd Corps, and the document states exactly what you just said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as document number 8 is concerned, since there is no translation, could you tell us who sent this document? Could you tell us the number of the document? And since it's a short document, perhaps you could read the entire document out loud.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is being sent, or was sent by the command of the Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond Central Bosnia central zone. It was sent to the HVO headquarters in Mostar. The number of the document is 1917/92. The date is the 29th of December, 1992. The time, 1730 hours. The title of the document is "Request for Agreement to Use Units." "In written request, dated the 28th of December, 1992, this command was contacted by the command of the 3rd Corps of the BH army, who requested that our units participate in offensive actions on the following axis: 1: Kobiljaca, Vela, Crkvice, Veliki Zovik; axis 2: Kobiljaca, Rakovica. In relation to the above, we request your agreement," signed by Colonel Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 9, do you recognise the document that you received as a response to your request?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do recognise this document, and it is a response to our request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I would now like to ask you about what happened as far as the HVO's attitudes towards the army is concerned after the corps was established. Did they continue to pursue the same activities that you have told us about, that you told us about yesterday, while you were the commander of the regional staff?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 3rd Corps of the BH army was formed, relations with the HVO became even more complicated, and there was the risk of a large-scale armed conflict breaking out with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look at document 0502, document number 2; 0505, document number 3; 0506 - this is all under section C - document number 4; DH513; document number 6 -- in fact, I think we've already had a look at that one. Yes, number 6, 0532. And could you tell me whether these documents confirm what you have just said? These documents from the HVO, which show that they continued to establish parallel organs of power - that can be see in DH505, for example - or rather, did they confirm that there was a zone of responsibility in which the 3rd Corps was operational. And in document DH513, did you inform your superior command of such problems?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise these documents, and that is what I was just speaking about a while ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at document number 6. This is a document from the Jure Francetic Brigade command. Could you tell me where the headquarters of this HVO brigade were located?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that the headquarters of this HVO brigade were located in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In item 1 of this order, the zone of responsibility of this brigade is established, is defined. General, could you tell me whether the brigade tried to take control of the main axis and the main strategic locations in the area of the 3rd Corps, which was around Zenica.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the strategic locations and strategic axis are around Zenica, which at the time was within the 3rd Corps zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is no translation of this document either. Therefore, I would like to ask the General to read out item number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could the General also tell us who signed the document and the title of the document. Who issued the document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is from the Jure Francetic Brigade command. The number of the document is 813/92. It is dated the 22nd of December, 1992. I think it's the 22nd. My copy is not very legible. I think the date is the 22nd of December, 1992. This order was signed by the president -- by the deputy commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade, Zoran Covic. It was signed personally by him. And the first item in the order is as follows: "An order to the 1st Battalion. The zone of responsibility will be as follows: The area of the town on the left bank of the River Bosna, Zenica, village of Cajdras, Vjetrenica road, the Kuber pass, the Lasva junction, the Lasvanska Petr, village of Drivusa, village of Raspotocje, Zenica road." That's the end of item 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Towards the end of 1992, immediately after the 3rd Corps had been established, were you able to observe that the Jure Francetic Brigade was establishing positions on the main roads around Zenica? And to what extent did this directly affect the combat situation of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This confirms the fact that the HVO in Zenica not only blocked the main roads from Zenica to the Lasva Valley, but the HVO also took over key strategic locations from which this entire area could be controlled. Since we can see this order, and in the field we managed to see that the HVO was taking such action, it was necessary for the 3rd Corps command to take the necessary counter-measures. As far as I can remember, we told the units in these parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina to remain in a state of readiness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you said that in 1992 there were two conflicts in the area of Gornji Vakuf. Tell me, what was the situation like in January 1993 in the area of Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of January 1993, the 3rd Corps was in the process of being formed. We had information, according to which the situation in Gornji Vakuf was extremely complex, and it was becoming more and more complex by the day. There were a number of incidents at some checkpoints, and the HVO in Gornji Vakuf deployed its units at elevated positions around the town of Gornji Vakuf. And as far as I can remember, a commission was formed to go to Gornji Vakuf to deal with the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, were you personally involved in trying to diffuse the situation in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was appointed as a representative of the BH army. I was part of a state organisation, formed of civilian organs of power and of certain military structures. It was a political and military delegation which went to Gornji Vakuf in order to negotiate there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given the situation, did the 3rd Corps commander and you yourself inform the superior command of the situation? Did you ask for instructions? Did you conduct yourselves in a responsible manner, as any responsible commander would have done?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed my superior of what was happening in Gornji Vakuf. I informed General Enver Hadzihasanovic, the 3rd Corps commander, of what was happening. I asked for assistance when dealing with the problem, because, if I'm not mistaken, about the 12th or 13th of January, the conflict escalated and an ultimatum was issued to me, requesting that the 3rd Corps units in the area of Gornji Vakuf surrender. I know that my superior, General Enver Hadzihasanovic, said that he could not authorise such a course of action, and he asked the superior command in Sarajevo for instructions as to how we should act. All I know is that at the time General Hadzihasanovic, my commander, ordered me to do all I could to prevent the conflict in Gornji Vakuf from escalating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, were you able to notice that in that area, in addition to the HVO forces from Gornji Vakuf and Bugojno, there were other, more numerous forces arriving from the wider area, the greater area of western Herzegovina, and even from other areas too?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the commander of the regional staff, as long back as 1992, I had information about the strength and the composition of the HVO unit in Gornji Vakuf. As for what was going on at that particular time, from the beginning of the conflict, I noticed that there was an increased number of tanks, that fire was being opened from heavy artillery. And my intelligence also told me that, in Gornji Vakuf, there were other units engaged, those that did not hail from Gornji Vakuf. Those were HVO units. So at that time I did not have reliable information as to what units those were and where they came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I would kindly ask you to look at the documents which are here listed under number 10, this is 0551; 11, 0552; 12, 0554; 13, 0555; 14, 0557; 15, 0558; 16, 0559; 17, 0561; 18, 0562; 19, 0564; 20, 0565; 21, 0566; 22, 0568; then the document under 27, 0576; number 28, 0577; number 29, 0578; number 30, 0581. Please look at number 32, 0589; Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond number 33, 0592; number 34, 0600. Can you also please look at number 35, 0604; number 36, 0615. Can you please look at number 40, 0620; and number 56, which is number 0705. Kindly look at these documents. But before that, can you tell me whether, at the end of their work, the task force that had been established, did they draft a report? And is this report the Defence Exhibit 56, bearing the Defence number 0705?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise all of these documents. These documents are orders, reports, and information clearly speaking of the situation in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of the documents, could you tell that they were also referring to you and the requests that you've already testified about, namely, that you asked for urgent instruction so as to avoid any further escalation of that conflict in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is precisely what these documents confirm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these documents also demonstrate that, in every request of yours, in every order and instruction issued by the commander of the 3rd Corps, a special emphasis is made on everything being done in order to avoid any further escalation of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said that, and these documents confirm it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document under number 21, although you have already seen it briefly. The Defence number is 0566. Tell me, did Commander Hadzihasanovic instruct all of his subordinate commands and brigades and warn them that these issues would be raised at the highest level, and that it would be President Izetbegovic and Dr. Franjo Tudjman who would have to make the final decisions on these issues.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise this document, and this is precisely what this document confirms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Such a behaviour on the part of the corps commander, namely, the fact that he asked all of his subordinates -- subordinate units to avoid any further conflict, the fact that he contacted his superior command asking for further instructions, the fact that he instructed his subordinate units to only use force when absolutely necessary, is such behaviour the kind of behaviour that would be demonstrated by a serious and responsible commander who found himself in a serious and demanding situation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have to confirm that. Yesterday during my testimony I was talking about the year 1992, and this goes on and repeats in 1993, only with the situation being even more complex. So Commander Hadzihasanovic found himself even in a more complex situation than I was in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us, General, that when you were in the field, you were given an ultimatum. Can you tell us, despite all of your efforts, how did the Croatian Defence Council behave in Central Bosnia? And what did this ultimatum mean at all?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I understood this ultimatum was that the units of the BH army had to place themselves under the command of the Croatian Defence Council, and that units of the Territorial Defence and units of the BiH army, in other words, all units of the 3rd Corps, had to be disarmed. I have to say that on behalf of the Croatian Defence Council, the delegation was headed by Colonel Zeljko Siljeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your response to that ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed my superior commander, because I did not have any authority to issue an order to the effect of the arms of the BiH army units in that area to be surrendered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a professional soldier, what was your assessment? Was it normal for an -- for a legitimate army to be given an ultimatum with such a tight deadline, for a legitimate army to be asked to surrender their weapons? How would a military, any other military, react to that, especially if such a ultimatum was given to them in their own country?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, the BiH army was at that time the armed force of the internationally recognised state of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and if anybody were to issue an ultimatum to disarm such a force, it would be absolutely preposterous, it would be absolutely unheard of. And every soldier would find it impossible to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a normal situation, every military force would launch a military reaction. You yourself went to great lengths to alleviate the situation and to avoid any conflict. Was that an additional problem to you as a commander, meaning how did you explain to your soldiers that you were willing to retreat before an ultimatum that was contrary to all the laws of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an impossible situation. At that time the 3rd Corps hadn't enough strength to even embark on an armed conflict with the Croatian Defence Council. But as I've already said, in our view, the opening of the second front line and the creation of a second enemy would have been very difficult for us, because we did not have any means or strength to put up resistance against one enemy, let alone two enemies at a time. It was almost impossible to explain that to our subordinate commanders. However, we tried to curb this conflict in Gornji Vakuf and prevent it from spreading into other areas of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let us be clear on that. When you said you had enough strength, and later on you said that you didn't have enough force, what did you mean? Did you mean that you did not have enough troops, or did you mean that you had ample troops and means to enter a conflict of that nature?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain. If we were to rally all the forces that were facing one enemy, we would have been able to put up a resistance against the other enemy. But at that time our main task was to defend ourselves against the aggression, and that means that at the time we did not have any means to militarily resolve the situation in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can you look at documents under number 23, this is DH47; number 24, DH2/ID; number 25, DH45; under number 26, DH46; under number 37, DH44/ID; under number 38, DH48. Can you please look at these documents which originate from the Croatian Defence Council. Tell me, please, while you're trying -- while you were trying to avoid any possible conflict, do these documents demonstrate a somewhat different behaviour on the part of the Croatian Defence Council, namely, that they gave you an ultimatum that they wanted to lead this army, and so on and so forth? Secondly, while you were in Central Bosnia, in the territory covered by the 3rd Corps, did you yourself experience these intentions of the Croatian Defence Council which wanted, at any cost, to gain control over one part of the territory of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I look at these documents, I can say that I recognise them as being documents issued by the Croatian Defence Council. They originate for various levels. I have to draw your attention to the fact that these documents are not documents that I saw during that particular period of time. Your Honours, I will have to go back, saying again and again, for one reason: When I testified before this Tribunal in the past, I had an occasion to see a number of documents issued by the Croatian Defence Council; however, the documents that I have before me at this moment show me that the Croatian Defence Council in Central Bosnia undertook activities aimed at gaining control over the territories that were mentioned in the political goals of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can you please look at document 23, which is DH47, which was issued by the administration of the military police. This document shows in its paragraph 3 that all cargo should be seized irrespective of the person that the cargo is intended for, and that members of the BH army should not be allowed to enter the area. Does this behaviour of the Croatian Defence Council, in January 1993, pose a threat only for Central Bosnia, or was it the kind of behaviour that posed a threat for the entire Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Tell me, the border crossings towards Croatia, were they the only channels via which food, arms, and any other necessities could enter Bosnia and Herzegovina? Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've managed to have a look at this document, and one may conclude that this meant a total blockade of Bosnia and Herzegovina, because it is a well-known fact that during that period of time, the only way the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina could exit its territory was via the Republic of Croatia. And if all those roads were blocked, this meant that the entire territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was under blockade, not only the territory of the 3rd Corps. And these measures were aimed not only against the members of the BH army but all the citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at document number 37, which is DH44/ID. Do you know which territory is depicted in this map?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map depicts one part of the municipality of Zenica, one part of the municipality of Vitez, and one part of the municipality of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Zivko Totic, who testified before this Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. And also one part of the municipality of Travnik. In other words, Zenica, Travnik, Vitez, and Busovaca, parts of these four municipalities. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A witness before this Trial Chamber, Zivko Totic, put these markings on this map based on the orders that he received on the 16th of January that we just saw a little while ago. In January 1993, General, did you witness the fact that the town of Zenica was encircled by the units of the Croatian Defence Council in this particular way?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a soldier, what can you tell us about the situation of Zenica and the BiH army? At the time the BiH army was stationed in Zenica and was supposed to go to the defence lines facing the Serbs from Zenica.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such a deployment on the part of the Croatian Defence Council disabled the BiH army to go to their positions facing the Serbs in the area. And there were cases when members of the BiH army were disarmed when they wanted to pass through the checkpoints established by members of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can you please tell me, did there come a time in January 1993 when the conflict in Central Bosnia spread? And if that was the case, can you tell me in what way did this conflict spread, and onto which areas?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second half of January, the conflict in Central Bosnia spread onto the municipality of Busovaca, the incidents when members of the BiH army were disarmed, those members from the brigade of BiH army in that territory of Busovaca and other activities undertaken by the HVO. And according to our intelligence, they were taking their most dominant points. And after the incident which took place at the checkpoint in Busovaca, all this led to an armed conflict which spread across the entire municipality of Busovaca in a very short time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can you please look at documents number 39, which is DH0619. Does this document speak about the beginning of these conflicts, the disarming of Muslim citizens and other incidents that you were aware of in 1993 and that you have just described for us? Since this document does not have a translation, can you please read who was it who drafted the document, what this document refers to, and can you please read the second paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was drafted by the command of the 3rd Corps. It bears number 02/33-202. The date is 22nd January 1993. The document was sent to the staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the BiH army in Sarajevo. This document was signed by Enver Hadzihasanovic. It was stamped. In the second paragraph of this document, one can read: "The ill-treatment of the Muslim population in Busovaca continues, as well as in Vitez, Novi Travnik, and other places. On the 21st of January, 1993, around 10.00 in the morning, at a checkpoint in the municipality of Busovaca, robbers in uniforms and insignia of the HVO seized a Mercedes owned by Beganovic from Zenica, who was then forced to cross the Lasva River. A similar case repeated when four passengers from Tesanj were armed from firearms. They were all Muslims."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document number 41 now, 1624, and then under 42, 1730. Since we don't have a translation for the second one, could you tell me who drafted the document, what is the document about, and could you read out the second and third sentence in the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise this document. It's a document from the 3rd Corps. You said it was document number 1730, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of the document is 02/31-142. It's dated the 24th of January, 1993. It's addressed to the Supreme Command staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Sarajevo. The second paragraph is as follows: "At about 1713 hours --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, but could you read out the two last sentences in the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "However, in the UNPROFOR column, there was an armoured personnel carrier and an HVO jeep. The personnel carrier opened fire on the positions of the members of the ABiH army. Fire was returned, and on that occasion two members of the HVO in the jeep were killed and the personnel carrier drove off."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please have a look at document number 43 now; the number of the document is 0631. And then number 45; 1734 is the number of that document. Since there's no translation for this document either, could you just tell us a little about the document. Give us the basic information. Who drafted it, and what's the date of the document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first document that you have mentioned is document number 0631. It's a document from the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have the translation of that document. But as far as document 44 is concerned, document number 1735, and document 45, which is document 1734, could you just tell me who drafted the document, could you tell me about the date, and who signed these two documents.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Document 1735, the first document, was issued by the 3rd Corps command. It's a combat report from the Supreme Command staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it was signed by Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic. The second document is document number 1734. It was issued by the 3rd Corps command, and it's an order to the command of the 333rd Mountain Brigade and to the 2nd Battalion of the 17th Krajina Brigade. It is signed by Enver Hadzihasanovic. In fact, I signed the document on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the break, could you have a look at document 46. We don't have a translation of this document. Could you tell me who issued this document, and could you read out item 4 in this order.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document from the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. The number is 01-167-SB/93. It is dated the 25th of January, 1993. This is an order signed by Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. I can't see his signature, though. Item 4 is as follows: "Destroy the Zenica-Busovaca road, and defend the obstacle with all available means."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, with regard to this document, I would like you to tell us whether this road, the Zenica-Busovaca-Vitez-Travnik road, because it's a road to both places, was this road -- did this road collapse, was it destroyed, and was it possible to use this road -- was it possible for members of the BH army to use this road in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I personally noticed that the road had been damaged and no one could use the road at that time. The BH army couldn't use it, nor could anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps we could have our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a quarter to 4.00. It's time for our break. We'll resume at about 10 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now resume. But before we continue with examining the witness, the Chamber would like to ask the Defence to inform the Chamber how they will use the time that remains for them in order to address issues other than those that concern the relations with the HVO or the structure of the BH army, because you have so far used up half of your time, and it's Tuesday, 4.20. We haven't yet addressed the substantial issues so we are somewhat concerned. Could the Defence provide us with some clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I think that perhaps in the next half an hour, or 45 minutes at the most, I'll be able to conclude the issue of the relations with the HVO. And I think I'll be able to deal with the General's knowledge of Dusina and the events in Dusina by the end of the day. On Thursday, I intend to move on to other matters that the General is personally familiar with, Miletici, Maline, Guca Gora, and, to a certain extent, the issue of the presence of foreigners in the area of the 3rd Corps. The relations that we have discussed are important, but as for what the General knows about specific events that relate to counts in the indictment, this is a field that we would perhaps embark on after the second break. And I think that we'll have more time to deal with these matters on Thursday. But the relations with the HVO are important, because other issues arise from these relations, which is why we've used about half of our time on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you've already spoken about the conflicts in January and about the relations that developed, the attempts to prevent an escalation of tension between the army and the HVO. Tell me whether, during that period of time, there were incidents of violating international humanitarian law by the HVO. What do you know about the attitude towards the civilian population, about the attitude towards individuals who were arrested? What do you know about such events in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I knew, the HVO, or rather, members of the HVO, or it would be better to say, individuals from the HVO, violated international humanitarian law. We, from the 3rd Corps, informed the international community of the fact. And I know that the international community became aware of the fact that international humanitarian law was being violated by members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at documents under 48, 51, and 61. 0653 is number 48; 51 is 0659; and number 61 is 0762. The first two documents are from the HVO. Do they confirm what you knew about that period? And document 61 is the result of the Joint Commission's investigation into damaged buildings in Busovaca, and it refers to the buildings that had been destroyed in the course of the events in Busovaca. General, do these documents reflect what you knew about the attitude of the HVO towards the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was present in the area and was able to take stock of this situation, together with representatives of the international community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the international community. General, at any point in time, given the escalation of the conflict in Busovaca, did the international community create some sort of a body whose responsibility was to try to prevent the conflict from escalating and to try and deal with any conflict situations?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps command tried to contact the HVO in order to prevent the conflict from escalating in the territory of Busovaca municipality. When we failed in doing this, we also contacted the international community. At the time, in the area of Zenica, there was the European Monitoring Commission, and they became actively involved in forming a joint commission, the name of which was the Busovaca Joint Commission. It was composed of representatives of the international community, led by EU Mission Monitors; there were UNPROFOR members, Red Cross and UNHCR members, and members of other international organisations who were in the area. And on behalf of the BH army, I was the BH army's representative, as the head of the mission. And on the other side, on the HVO side, there was Franjo Nakic, who acted in the capacity of the deputy commander of the command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia; there was Tihomir Blaskic. That was the mixed Busovaca commission, the Joint Commission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, where did you meet? And were you free to go to the meetings of that commission?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Joint Commission had its headquarters in Busovaca. And I went to those meetings under UNPROFOR escort. I wasn't able to go there in any other way because of the combat in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, as a commission, was it possible for you to discuss various issues, and at the time was that, in fact, the only place where you, as an army representative, were able to complain on behalf of the army and have other bodies in the area under the control of the army?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time it was the only means of communication between the BH army and the HVO in that area, naturally, with the international community acting as a mediator. At those meetings we tried to put an end to the hostilities, we tried to render the situation normal, we tried to get the parties involved in the conflict to withdraw and to get the trenches filled in. But naturally we used this opportunity to inform each other. I would tell the HVO what was happening, how members of the BH army were being treated, how civilians who were being captured on a large scale were being treated. And I mentioned -- I was able to talk about people who weren't Croats, I was able to talk about how they were being treated in that area. This concerned the entire territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The HVO also took advantage of the opportunity to inform me about what was happening on the other side. They informed me of whether there were similar situations on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In response to my question about the work of the Busovaca commission -- well, as far as this issue is concerned, I'll put questions to you when I ask questions about the events in Dusina. But now, given the tension that was calmed down to an extent, tell me, after some time, the conflict escalated, and what was at stake? What happened, in fact?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the initial results of the Joint Commission in Busovaca were visible. The intensity of the clashes dropped. Up until the Washington agreement, an end wasn't put to the conflict, but from time to time there was more intense fighting in the Busovaca municipality. But in April 1993, there was a new problem. First there were some incidents, and then some clashes between the HVO and the BH army in the area of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the attitude of the BH army when these conflicts broke out? And did the army adopt a different perspective with regard to these events? Did it continue to try and find a way of avoiding an all-out conflict? Were attempts made to find a joint solution to the escalation of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH army, given the overall situation -- well, I must tell you what the main mission of the BH army was again, and this was also the mission of the 3rd Corps: It was to fight the aggressor. All the orders that we received from our superior command were issued in relation to this main mission. We didn't have sufficient forces to become engaged in some other battlefield, at some other front. We had insight into the overall policies of the BH republic, and that was to avoid conflict with the HVO at whatever the cost. And the 3rd Corps command, together with its commander, General Hadzihasanovic, made huge efforts to avoid such conflicts, or to ensure that such conflicts did not become even more intense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the HVO officially accept such attempts, or did they really accept such attempts? Or rather, how did the HVO act during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we took advantage of the existence of the Busovaca Joint Commission so that we could inform the HVO of the attitudes and the positions of the 3rd Corps. But this didn't bear any fruit, because from Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond day to day the fighting grew more and more intense, until a conflict broke out in the area of Vitez municipality. In the area of Vitez, the Busovaca Joint Commission, together with the international community, concluded that the focus of the commission should be transferred to the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April, in the fighting around Vitez, were there any events that put the 3rd Corps commander and all the commanders in a particular situation in which they had to calm soldiers down and prevent them from retaliating against HVO members? If that was the case, could you describe these events for us.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April, in the fighting in the area of Vitez municipality, there was a terrible tragedy. War crimes were committed on a very large scale. Relations between the BH army and the HVO deteriorated even more. The corps command again did everything it could to explain to its subordinates and to inform their superiors of the fact that the situation in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps was becoming increasingly complex. And it was very difficult to explain to a soldier who had lost all his family and lived in the municipality of Vitez that this is how one should act.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you then find out that the HVO, who officially said that they wanted to cooperate with you, was simultaneously establishing close cooperation with the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time we had intelligence, according to which the HVO was talking to and negotiating with representatives of the Republika Srpska army. And they were trying to agree on how they should act if the conflict in the Lasva Valley escalated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, towards the end of April and May, were additional efforts made at the highest political level, and then within the 3rd Corps too, to finally put an end to this conflict and to try and liberate the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina by using joint forces? If that was the case, could you tell us which bodies were formed, and what do you personally know about all of this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the way that the situation developed in the Lasva Valley, as far as I know, at the time I had information, according to which there were political talks at the highest level in Zagreb between representatives of the BH government, or including representatives of the BH government. And it was agreed that a joint command should be formed so that the forces of the BH army, acting together with the HVO forces, fought the aggressor in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become involved in some of the bodies of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the area of the Lasva Valley, a joint command was formed composed of representatives from the BH army and HVO representatives. As I was appointed as head of the BH army, as their representative, and as an HVO representative, Mr. Franjo Nakic, was appointed by an order issued from -- by the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, Tihomir Blaskic. The headquarters were to be in Travnik, in the post office building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, at the time did you become seriously engaged in a task? Where were you located? And were you monitoring the situation in Travnik and in the Bila valley?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I took this task very seriously, and I believed that these high-level political agreements would bear fruit. And I thought that the tactical and operations level would be able to agree on joint action against the aggressor in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I believed that our combined force would be used to fight the aggressor in Bosnia and Herzegovina. During that period, I, as a representative of the BH army, or rather, Franjo Nakic, as the representative of the HVO, we, in that joint command, had very good information on what was happening in the Lasva Valley and around the Lasva Valley. Naturally, the international community helped us a lot, together with the European Monitors and UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The existence of this joint command, did it solve the problems that had escalated before? What was the position of the army at that time? Was it allowed a free passage through the Bila valley and the Lasva Valley, or did you witness a somewhat different situation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that the joint command had been established, in military terms, it could not function. Let me just give you one example to prove that. This joint command did not have any communications means, so we could not function as a true command, in the true sense of that word, in the sense command functions in modern armies. However, we tried as much as we could to draft a plan for joint operations. We failed, however, because the situation deteriorated by the day, and our attention, instead of being channeled towards the aggressor, had to be channeled towards problems in the Lasva Valley because of the new checkpoints springing up, new incidents occurring, and their numbers getting bigger by the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at a series of documents testifying to the behaviour of the HVO and the BiH army - you have just testified about that - and those documents are number 64, 0857; number 65, 0858; number 66, 0878; number 67, 0894; 68, 0927; number 69, 0930; number 70, 0935; number 71, 0937; number 72, 0940; 73, 0964; number 74, 0966; number 75, 0991; number 76, 0997; number 79, 1067; number 80, 1859; number 81, 1108. I know that you don't have much time. Please look at the documents. My questions are as follows: Do these documents reflect part of the behaviour, on the one hand, of the BH army, and, on the other hand, of the Croatian Defence Council during that period of time between April and June?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a set of documents drafted by both the HVO and by the BiH army, as well as the documents issued by the joint command from Travnik. They all speak of the situation deteriorating. They say that members of the HVO continued blocking the roads, they continued blocking the passage of BiH army units. They speak of the HVO taking elevation points around Travnik. Here there is a document testifying to the shelling of Travnik, a document testifying to the cooperation with the aggressor, all of the things that I have already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the record, I would like to state that among these documents, 0878, 0927, 0935, there are documents without translation, and the Defence will endeavour to have these documents translated by the end of the testimony of this witness so as to enable the Trial Chamber to inform themselves of these documents before putting their questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have just told us that some of these documents demonstrate the cooperation between the HVO and the Serbian forces. Can you please look at the documents numbered 77, bearing the Defence number 1030; number 82, bearing number 1123; document number 83, bearing number 1124; number 84, 1130; number 85, 1133. Since you have told us that you had intelligence testifying to the cooperation between the HVO and the army of Republika Srpska, my first question would be whether these documents confirm whatever intelligence you had at the time. Second question: Did this put the BH army in a situation to change its defence plans? In other words, did they now assume that they would have to put up a defence against two enemies at the time?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously every command has to assess the current situation and plan according to these assessments. Based on the intelligence that we had at the time already in April, we had to draft different plans of defence in the territory of the 3rd Corps. We had various plans. One of them envisaged the attack by just one aggressor; the other envisaged a simultaneous attack by the aggressor and the HVO. There were all different variations, which is only normal in the process of the work of any one command. Our intelligence that we had at the time is confirmed by these documents. What we had at the time was confirmed in practice. During Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond these periods, we saw that the HVO was acting in concert with the Serbian aggressor, with the army of Republika Srpska. They abandoned their position facing the aggressor and ceding these positions to the aggressor. This made the situation in the territory of the 3rd Corps even more complex. These are the indicators that the Serbian aggressor, or the army of Republika Srpska, was acting together with the HVO. This was the worst situation that we could envisage, and it was already in place in mid-June. And the 3rd Corps was facing an extremely difficult situation. At the beginning, we didn't know how to deal with that terrible situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, since you were a member of this joint command, and you acted in the territory of Travnik, can you please tell me, the documents demonstrate various problems that the army had to face at the time, one of them being the total blockade. What was the situation at the Bila valley? What was the situation that the 306th Mountain Brigade faced in the Bila valley? In this regard, can you please look at document number 80, bearing the defence number 1859.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Together with UNPROFOR, and together with a representative of the Croatian Defence Council, Mr. Franjo Nakic, I had an occasion to visit some parts of the Bila valley. I did it on several occasions. And together with Franjo Nakic, I convinced myself that all the roads were totally blocked. When you look at the map, and when you see where those obstacles were and where the positions of the HVO were at the time, you can conclude, as I could at the time, that the 306th Brigade was in very dire straits. Its position was very difficult because it was completely intersected. It was so intersected that, for example, the company commands could not cooperate. They were completely broken up. The battalions could not communicate. The brigade command could not link up with anybody else in the Bila region. We had a case that I want to share with you. The command of the 306th Brigade was very close at the time to the Croatian defence lines in the building of the mine, and it was directly exposed to the fire opened by the HVO. We had a situation that a member of the army was killed in the headquarters of the command. Together with UNPROFOR, we inspected the site where this happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I showed you the document number 8C - this is number 1859, the date is 30 May 1993, and this order shows -- do you have this document before you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This shows that the 306th Brigade was completely broken up and encircled in the villages which are mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document confirms precisely that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, just briefly tell us what is your information about the developments in June 1993. The situation when the main elevation points had been taken by HVO, when the BH army was completely broken up, did it lead to certain conflicts in Travnik and the Bila valley?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The efforts on the part of the joint command to resolve the situation in the Bila valley and Travnik at the beginning of June 1993 failed, and the Croatian Defence Council took up the main elevation point. Very strange situations took place, and we could not find any solution to these situations. For example, at the beginning of June, the commander of the operations group, the commander of the brigade were arrested. Members of the brigade command and the battalion command were put in a very difficult situation. They were disarmed. And all of a sudden one didn't know how to react to these strange situations. At the beginning of June 1993, Travnik was shelled. I was in Travnik at the time, I was in the post office building, and I could see the first shells falling around the post office building, around the barracks, and in other parts of the town of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Simultaneously with these military activities, during this period of time, did HVO engage in some propaganda activities aimed at portraying the BiH army, in the eyes of the world, in a different way, in a way different than the one you advocated and fostered? Did they start introducing a certain name for you who were members of the BH army, a name that was first used unofficially and then it became the official way members of the BiH army were addressed? Are you aware of that? Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had an opportunity on several occasions to talk to members of the HVO. They started using the words "Muslim armed forces." They started addressing me as the deputy commander of the Muslim armed forces. They started addressing me as a Mujahedin, as an Arab. I don't know what other names they used. They accused me of being an aggressor against the Croatian people; they accused me of wanting to destroy the Croatian people. There were some official meetings, and they said that they were talking to representatives of the Muslim forces. We protested. We said that we didn't -- we were not the command of any Muslim forces, that we were not the command of the Muslim armed forces; we said that we were the command of the 3rd Corps of the BiH army. There were also situations at official meetings when the HVO addressed members of the Supreme Command as commanders of the Muslim forces. I remember one situation which took place in mid-June when a representative of the Main Staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Stjepan Siber, was addressed as commander of the Muslim forces, and General Siber obviously protested against such observations. I also had occasions to hear in the media the HVO always said that they were being attacked by the Muslim forces; that the Muslim forces wanted to subdue them, to destroy them, to launch an aggression against the Croatian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at document number 86, bearing number 1175. Tell me, please, is this one of the documents that confirms the things that you have just testified about?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is very clear that under item 1 of this document, it is not the term "army" that is being used. The term being used is "the Muslim forces."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the attack on Travnik and the fighting in Travnik, did this spread on to the Bila valley? Were there any attacks and fighting in the Bila valley?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information that we had in the joint command in Travnik, the conflict between the BiH army and the HVO, which started in the town of Travnik, was spreading. And when you look at the map, you can see that this conflict was spreading on to the Bila valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since we will have to go back to the conflict in the Bila valley, I would like to ask you now: After these combat activities in the Bila valley, did the Croatian Defence Council, during the month of June, independently, or together with the Serbian forces, attack some other strategic areas where units of the 3rd Corps could be found?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously we monitored the developments very closely, especially on the defence lines facing the Serbian aggressor.
