And we had the intelligence, according to which similar situations and things were happening in other areas where the contact between the HVO and the aggressor against the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina were very obvious, and especially those contacts were very close with the representatives of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what happened in Kakanj? And I would also like you to provide us with some more details as to what problems did the 3rd Corps face in the area of Zepce. And also, what was the strategic value of Zepce and Maglaj, not only for the 3rd Corps but for the entire defence of the entire Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first half of June 1993, we had combat activities around Travnik and in the Bila valley. There were also incidents at the same time, or approximately around the same time, in Kakanj. We had information that at the HVO checkpoints there, members of the BiH army were being stopped, that the civilians were being arrested, that the Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond Croatian Defence Council was behaving very badly towards members of the BiH army. And soon after the first incidents at the checkpoints, there was an escalation of this conflict in the territory of Kakanj. As far as I can remember, this all was taking place sometime around the 8th of June. On the 11th of June, we had a fully blown conflict in the territory of Kakanj. So on the 10th, 11th, and 12th of June, this was all happening. The subsequent information told us that the situation in Maglaj and Zepce was very complex. The Croatian Defence Council already cooperated and negotiated with the army of Republika Srpska about joint activities. And the blockade was lifted from the general area of Bosnia and Herzegovina around Maglaj, around Tesanj, and one part of Teslic. All this was a very strategic area, a very strategic territory. And the command of the 3rd Corps, at that time, in the month of June, was given the mission to channel all of its forces towards lifting the blockade from this area, irrespective of the fact that Maglaj and Tesanj were not in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. However, once you received a task, you have to follow through. The corps command was still in a situation which was getting more complex by the day, and this was an impossible situation for the command of the 3rd Corps. The commander of the 3rd Corps received his task, moved his command post towards Zepce in order to be as close to the area where his next task was going to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in view of all of these developments that you have just briefly described for us, were you yourself engaged in the attempt to resolve the situation in Kakanj, in the attempt to set up joint commands there? And what were the results of all of these efforts?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps command and myself really made great efforts to find a solution, to reach an agreement, because we knew that if a new front was opened facing the HVO, we, as soldiers, would find ourselves in an impossible situation. The width of the front that we had, the length of the front that we had before, well, it was over -- it was several hundred kilometres long; sometimes it was between 450 and 500 kilometres long. We had a long line facing the aggressor. And if we were to open a new front, the line would be even longer. We were in an impossible situation. Through Catholic members of the clergy, we tried to influence the HVO and the Croatian population. We tried to ensure that a conflict was avoided. We tried to avoid casualties. But naturally, we weren't very successful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, since, throughout that period of time, in the 3rd Corps area, there were peace forces that were present - UNPROFOR, the European Monitors, et cetera - did you also contact them and inform them of the problems with the HVO? Did you ask them to become involved to ensure that agreements were respected?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout this period of time, we tried to obtain the help of all the UN organisations in that area, or rather, we tried to obtain the help of the international community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now ask you to go through the following documents under section D. Could you have a look at the documents 1 to 39. And could you tell me whether this is how you tried to inform the other party in the conflict, and especially the international community, of everything that was happening in that area.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've had a look at all these documents, and they do confirm what I was just saying a minute ago. I've seen some documents that were sent both to the international community and to the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, to the command of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would now like to move on to certain specific events referred to in the indictment. With the help of the usher, could the Chamber and members of the Prosecution be provided with another series of documents, these documents which I want to show to the witness, and they relate to Dusina and Miletici. This time we didn't discriminate against our colleagues from the Prosecution; we have managed to use tabs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you have heard, I would like to talk to you about the knowledge you have of certain events that relate to the counts in the indictment in this case. General, tell me whether you ever heard about allegations of crimes having been committed in the village of Dusina.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first time I heard about crimes that may have been committed in the village of Dusina was at a meeting. I obtained this information from Colonel Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who attended the meeting, and where was the meeting held?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the events and the combat in Busovaca, in an attempt to end the fighting in Busovaca, and as suggested by the international community, a meeting was held in Kiseljak, on the 26th of January, 1993. It was in the UNPROFOR command in Kiseljak. And there were representatives of the BH army and HVO representatives; the international community acted as a mediator. At that time I was the representative of the BH army, and Tihomir Blaskic was the HVO representative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who the representatives of the international community were at the time?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main representative of the international community at the meeting was General Cordy-Simpson, if I'm not mistaken. I think he's an Englishman. I don't know what his position was in the UNPROFOR command in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the main objective of the meeting? What were you supposed to agree on? What were you supposed to reach an agreement on when these discussions between the army and the HVO were held?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were to agree on putting an end to the fighting in Busovaca; we were to agree on finding a peaceful solution to the conflict, which already seemed to be turning into a large-scale conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any success in trying to establish a cease-fire before Colonel Blaskic informed you of the allegations about the crimes?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reached Kiseljak and Zenica in an armoured personnel carrier from the UNPROFOR BritBat, which was located in Vitez at the time. The trip from Zenica to Kiseljak was difficult, especially when passing through Busovaca municipality where fighting was ongoing. We started the meeting in Kiseljak, but towards the end of the meeting, Colonel Blaskic informed us of the information he had received on the crimes committed in Dusina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The information that you were provided with by Colonel Blaskic, did this information affect the way the meeting developed? And was there an agreement on signing a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could assess the situation at the time, that was the key information that was provided. Although towards the end of the meeting, we had almost managed to agree on a cessation of hostilities. They were prepared to sign such a document. But Colonel Blaskic refused to continue working at the meeting. I remember very well that at the time General Cordy-Simpson tried to ensure that the meeting came to an end, and tried to ensure that a cease-fire was signed, but Colonel Blaskic wouldn't agree to this. And the meeting came to an end on the 26th of January, 1993, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go after the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting, in the afternoon, I returned to the 3rd Corps command in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you inform Commander Hadzihasanovic of what had happened at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time I provided the 3rd Corps command and General Hadzihasanovic with a detailed report on what had happened. Naturally, I said that the meeting would continue the following day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When preparing for the meeting that was to be held on the following day, did you and the commander request that all the reports on the situation in Dusina be provided to you? And did you have the opportunity of seeing what subordinate units had reported to you with Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond regard to the events?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the corps commander immediately informed the superior command of the events in Kiseljak, and naturally within the corps we took measures to find out what was happening at the time in the village of Dusina. We received reports a little later, because communication links were very poor. As I have said, it was very difficult for us to contact units in the field. And I know that the units that were in the field found it very difficult to establish contact with its first superior command, with its immediate superior command. So the reports we received on that day showed that, in the area of Dusina, there was fighting. Individuals had been killed on both sides; the HVO and the BH army had sustained casualties. There was fighting, and men were killed on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you now have a look at the documents under number 14, P251.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please refer to these numbers a little more slowly, because I don't have all the references here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, the wrong documents were shown to the witness. I think we have solved the problem now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was referring to the document under number 14, Exhibit P251. This is a document that the Zenica municipal defence staff provided to the regional staff in Zenica, the regional defence staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me whether this confirms what you, in fact, knew; namely, that there was fighting in that area and that casualties were sustained by both sides.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What you said is, in fact, confirmed in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document number 16, P130.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've had a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this document also refer to the disposition in the combat zone, and does it refer to fighting?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a regular combat report, and it does refer to combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document number 17 now; that's document P131.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've had a look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this document also forwarded to the operations centre of the 3rd Corps, and is this one of the documents that you examined, together with the commander, that shows that there was combat?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document 19, please, P200. It's also a document from the Zenica region, and it also refers to combat but in a somewhat different way.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've had a look at the document. And it is from the regional staff. It's addressed to the 3rd Corps command, to the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, although we have already seen similar documents, yesterday we were discussing whether you had a military position or not. At the end of the document your name is printed. But who would sign the document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dugalic Ramiz, and it says "For the commander, Dugalic Ramiz." Yesterday I tried to explain such situations. I didn't have a dual role. I was the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps at the time, because the regional defence staff had not yet been disbanded. I wouldn't go into this again, but if the Chamber has any other questions, I could clarify the issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document number 22, Exhibit P346. This is also a document from the Zenica region. The signature is the same. It's addressed to the 3rd Corps. Does this document also mention the fact that in the area of Dusina there was fighting and casualties were sustained by both sides?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document confirms that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look at document number 26 now, P828. It's a report from the 7th Muslim Brigade to the duty operations centre in the 3rd Corps. Does this document also reflect the situation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document also confirms what you were just saying and what I have already testified about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to one of my questions a while ago, you said that communications were fairly poor, and you said that information would arrive a little too late sometimes. In this document, although the same day is concerned, the description of the events is different. In the previous document we had a look at, reference was made to an HVO attack and the Bosniak population being arrested, whereas the other document states what is said in documents from the 7th Muslim Brigade and in documents from the municipal staff. Tell me, given the poor communications at the time, was it possible for reports from certain commands to be inaccurate? Was it, therefore, necessary to carry out further verifications or wait for additional reports? Were there such situations as far as your units and command in January 1993 are concerned?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These situations -- such things did occur in the field. Apart from the fact that there were poor communications at all levels of control and command - and I've spoken about this already in detail - but I would also like to inform the Chamber or remind the Chamber of a very important factor, something that I mentioned yesterday, and this factor concerns the level of training of our members of staff. If you have someone who's involved in communications but isn't trained in military terms, he's not a very well-educated person, in such cases it's very difficult for such an individual to provide a clear combat report in accordance with the standards of the 3rd Corps. So we have two important problems here, and I mentioned them yesterday: The problem of communications and the problem of the level of qualifications of the staff members who forward information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said when you informed General Hadzihasanovic, who was the commander of the 3rd Corps at the time, when you informed him about what had happened in the meeting, he informed the superior command. Could you please have a look at document 18 now, P133. No, I apologise, it's -- P133, yes. A 3rd Corps document dated the 26th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've looked at the document, although I found it very difficult to find this number at the bottom. Normally all these numbers are on the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you sure that it was 11?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, not 11, 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle paragraph, you can see that Commander Hadzihasanovic is informing the Supreme Command staff of what had occurred during the meeting. Is this a document which truthfully conveys the message that you had given to Commander Hadzihasanovic after you returned from this meeting in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of your general military experience as an officer, could you tell the Trial Chamber whether the truthful informing on the part of the Supreme Command on any information they may have is one of the major elements of the responsible performance of the commander's duties.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is a principle that any commander should respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to stop here because it is 25 to 6.00. We are going to make a break, and we shall resume around 1800 hours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give the floor to the Defence. You may repeat the question that you put to the witness just before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, before the break, I put a question to you which I'm now going to repeat. I would kindly ask you to tell me, as a professional officer, what was your professional military experience with regard to the reporting? Is truthful reporting of a superior command one of the important characteristics and responsibilities of the commander which show that this commander is responsible in the exercise of his duties?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report, which was spent to the superior command by the commander of the 3rd Corps, is truthful, and it was drafted in the way I reported to the commander of the 3rd Corps, General Hadzihasanovic. And it shows the character of this commander. It is true, what you have just said, that one of the important characteristics of every commander is truthful reporting to the superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document number 20, which is P211; number 21, P212; and number 25, which is P237. These are three reports to the staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces. Tell me first, in the command of the 3rd Corps, was there a defined way of reporting? Do these documents, when you look at them, represent a meeting of the obligation on the part of the 3rd Corps to send all the information to its superior command within a given period of time?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a customary procedure within the system of command and control. The documents that you have just shown me confirm precisely that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where would the information from the field arrive in the command of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information from the field from the duty operations officers of the subordinate unit would arrive in the duty operations centre of the 3rd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The operations centre, or the duty operations officer, is that the person that prepares information for the superior command? In practice, is there such a situation in which the information from the duty operations centre, signed by the commander of that command, goes to the superior command without the signatory of this report seeing this information?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain briefly the so-called regular reports and interim reports. The 3rd Corps of the BH army tried to honour this customary procedure. Regular reports which are drafted in the operations centre can be daily reports or can be interim combat reports. They are sent to the superior command, and they have to be given to the commander if the commander is at the command, because reports should not be sent to the superior command with any delay. When the corps commander is absent, this information has to be checked by the person that is standing in for the corps commander at the time. Those were mostly his deputy, which was myself, the Chief of Staff, and very rarely it did occur that these three persons were not at the command, they were not able to check those reports that were sent to the superior command. There are such reports that the commander himself may sign and directly send to the superior command, which is left to the commander's assessment and up to him to decide whether to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were informed about the combat report of the 7th Muslim Brigade, which reached you through the normal channels, and when you were informed about other reports that came from the municipal staff and the regional defence staff of Zenica, in this particular concrete situation, was it normal for the 3rd Corps to receive the reports on the same events from the resubordinated units, as well as the report from that command to which one part of this unit was resubordinated in this specific case and for this specific combat mission?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the system of command and control, if this system functions normally, and if this system is equipped with all the necessary equipment, and if it is professionally staffed, then it would not be possible for such a thing to happen. However, I already said yesterday that our personnel was not trained, that our means of communications were very poor. So it would be possible for the second subordinate to send a report to his superior who is at a higher level. This could happen, but it was not part of the customary practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you were at the meeting in Kiseljak, and especially when you looked at all the combat reports, did you at all know what was going on in the area of Lasva? Did you know why these forces were deployed in the area of Lasva in the first place?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that combat activities in Busovaca, on the 25th of January, were of such proportions that they gave rise for concern. On the 25th, the Croatian Defence Council had a significant tactical advantage, had a lot of successes in the field. They took some of the facilities which were in the territory of Busovaca municipality. And already during that period, all members of the army were either arrested or expelled from the town, and the Croatian Defence Council had a lot of successes in two technical positions, or on two technical axes; one followed the Lasva Valley towards Zenica, and the second axis was south from that axis. Obviously, from the field we received very unfavourable information, and it was normal for the command to take measures in order to strengthen the defence lines in those areas. According to my intelligence, the intention was to occupy the Lasva junction and to intersect the main road from Zenica towards other places in the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can we please now look at document number 3, which is Prosecution document number 406 [Realtime transcript read in error "46"], dated 19th January, which is the time, as you have testified earlier, when the conflict escalated and when you received this ultimatum from the Croatian Defence Council. Line 18 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction, it is not 46 but 406.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What number is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 3. Let me first ask you: Is this the reaction of the 3rd Corps commander to the ultimatum that was given to you? When was the deadline of the ultimatum; can you remember? The ultimatum that was given to you by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was around the 15th. But in any case, it was before the 19th of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this order the reaction, or the normal reaction of the 3rd Corps command? Is it normal for them to deploy their forces in order to prevent the attack of the HVO on these areas?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a normal reaction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you've already told us something about the Lasva junction and its significance, can you please look at item 10 in this order. I would like the usher's assistance in providing you with a map, and I'm going to ask you to show us on this map what was the task as specified in item 10 of this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness has been provided with a part of the map that has already been admitted. The title is "Dusina - Set 4." This is a part of the map Zenica 4, 1:50.000. At the same time I would like the General to be provided with another map. For the record, this is from the set 3 of the maps that have already been admitted. This -- the part of Zenica 144, 1:100.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just for the record, as the maps are being distributed, I note on the 1:50.000 map, that the village of Dusina has been highlighted with an oval. I don't believe that was on the previous version of the map. We don't have an objection to this, but simply for the record, we indicate that that has been highlighted on the map, as provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have noticed that. The Defence is going to explain why is that the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know what to say, Your Honours. Today we have requested for these two maps to be taken from the set of maps, since the title Zavjetnica [phoen] and Dusina, it is for that reason that these two places have been marked specially. I have these maps on A4 format, and there are no markings on them. If there's a problem, I can provide the witness with my copies. And it is obvious that this is not part of the original map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we don't have an objection. I just simply note that for the record, because my learned colleague has indicated that this is part of a map that's previously in evidence, and I don't believe those markings were on the map as it was previously admitted. So just simply to avoid any confusion on down the road, we simply wanted to put that on the record. We have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And just for the record, since my technical knowledge is very modest, my colleague has just warned me that the main places referred to in here are marked on the CD programme. We can have them removed tomorrow. But I believe that with these explanations, the map will be of use to you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask the witness to take the map 1:100.000, also to take a marker, and mark the places where the municipal staff of Zenica and one company of the 7th Muslim Brigade were deployed. It is being deployed on a certain line. Can you please mark those places mentioned under item 10. Can you mark them on this map, obviously, if you can see them. Before that, can you please put a circle around the Lasva junction, and can you put number 1 next to that circle.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's the village of Guvna [phoen] here.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gumanci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark the location of that village. You could encircle it and mark it with number 2.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Saracevica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Saracevica is on the map.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Defence number 3 marks the location of Saracevica. Kuber.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kuber is a wider area. We have this elevation. It's at 860 metres above sea level, if I can see this correctly. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have marked Kuber with number 4. Could you mark the location of Vjetrenica now.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vjetrenica has been marked with number 5. And could you mark the location of Vranjaca.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's number 6. I don't know whether it can be seen here, but elevation 952, Ovnak, perhaps you can find it.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm marking the area of Ovnak. But as for elevation 952, I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But mark the area of Ovnak with number 7.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you tell me, where the units of the municipal Territorial Defence staff deployed, which were supported by one company of the 7th Muslim? In which area were they deployed in relation to the local commune of Vranjaca or, rather, in relation to the village of Dusina? Were they deployed in the area of Dusina?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The disposition of the forces is towards the north-west from the village of Dusina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What separates these positions from the area in which Dusina is located? Is there a mountain, a river, or something like that, which in fact separates these two areas?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. There is a river, and there is a road that passes through the Lasva Valley, or rather, passes along the Lasva River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Keep the maps with you. We might be needing them later. But have a look at document number 4 now, Exhibit P479. It's a document from the 7th Muslim Brigade. In military terms, is this a normal sort of order which is a result of the previous order on their resubordination? I draw your attention to item 2.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's quite normal. The sequence is quite normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at the document under number 5, Exhibit P236. It's dated the 22nd of January, 1993. Have a look at item 3 in the order and tell me what the attitude of the 3rd Corps, or rather, of the command of the 3rd Corps was with regard to the deployment of forces in this area.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite clearly his position that defence positions should be taken and fire should not be opened without authorisation from the superior command, or rather, the units should not go into action on their own initiative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look at document number 6, P310. Is this a normal report of the subordinate command to the corps which informs them of carrying out -- which informs them of the implementation of some of their tasks?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They're reporting on the fact that units have assumed their positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document number 7, P825. Have a look at item 2. And does this document also provide information, according to which the subordinate unit under the command of the Zenica municipal defence staff is, in fact, subordinated, as ordered?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's under number 7. It's a regular combat report from the 7th. For the sake of the transcript, the exhibit number is P825. You can't see that number on the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what is clearly stated in item 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document number 8, P210. And could you first tell me who this document is addressed to?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 8. It's a document dated the 23rd of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is the number P210?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is the document addressed to?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is addressed to municipal defence staffs in Zenica and in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the municipal defence staffs resubordinated to the command of the 3rd Corps at that time?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were part of that corps, but they weren't directly resubordinated to the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you said yesterday, at the time there was a regional staff too, and it was through the regional staff that they were connected to the 3rd Corps, that they were linked to the 3rd Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During this period of time, that was the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the map that we had a look at a minute ago, could you just mark with the felt tip the axis assigned to the Kakanj municipal staff. Perhaps it's not visible on the map, but could you just indicate this axis with an arrow, if possible. Could you indicate the line that the Kakanj staff was supposed to secure, if it's visible on the map. If not, we have a different map.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the valley of the River Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark the location of the River Bosna?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll have to mark it in the opposite direction, because Kakanj is in the opposite direction of the River Bosna. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just indicate it with an arrow so that we know that that is the axis that the Kakanj municipal staff had to secure. Tell me, what sort of task was assigned to the Zenica municipal staff? What does it say under item number 2 in this order? Could you draw a line indicating this route referred to in the order. Perhaps it would be better to use the map of the scale which is 1:50.000.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can do it on this map. You can see the features indicated in item 2 of the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you draw a line indicating these features.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps the line you have just drawn, perhaps you could put a number in the middle of the line, number 8. This indicates the line referred to in this order, P210.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've already spoken about an HVO document, and the document said that it was necessary to obstruct a road in the Lasva Valley. Can you indicate the area where the main road in the Lasva Valley was obstructed, which made it impossible to reach Busovaca, or rather, Vitez.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark that location with number 9.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the sake of the transcript, let's say that number 9 represents the site where the road through the Lasva Valley was completely obstructed. General, line number 8 referred to in this order, or route number 8, was that the only route that could be used to go from Zenica via the Lasva junction to the free territory in the area of Busovaca and Kacun? Or were there any other routes that units and the population might use?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, this was the only route connecting these areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now have a look at document number 9, P199. Again, this is an order from the Zenica regional defence staff. As you have already said, was this a document signed by the acting commander of the regional staff?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at item 3. Does this order follow on an order from the 3rd Corps, according to which units should be deployed as ordered by the corps commander; and these units should not be used or should not go into action unless they were first attacked?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document number 10, P127. The date is the 24th of January. Tell me, what sort of position did the corps commander adopt with regard to the possibility conflicts? It's in item 2 that this is referred to. The date of the document is the 24th of January, 1993, as we see.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order on agreement, in principle, on the cease-fire and on the separation of the BH army forces and the HVO units and cessation of hostilities with the HVO. Further on it says: "Do not initiate any conflicts until further notice. The previously issued orders are still in force." In the third item of the order, it states that the commander of the 3rd Corps should immediately be informed of incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, use the previous map, the scale of which is 1:100.000, and could you mark it with today's date and could you sign it. And then I'll ask you to have a look at the other map that you have before you.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're going to have to tell me the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it's the 7th.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please place the map, the scale of which is 1:50.000, on the ELMO. And have a look at document number 11, P128. Before I ask you something about this document, you said that one day before, and over that period of time, the HVO had penetrated in certain areas. Tell me, what sort of situation was Merdani in?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Merdani was on the main axis of attack of the HVO in the direction of the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can see Merdani on the map, could you please mark it with a cross.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Either a cross or a circle, and mark it with number 1.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look at the order I have just referred to, P128. And could you tell me -- could you draw the line referred to in item 1, which states that "a reinforced company from the 303rd Mountain Brigade shall move towards Zenica-Lasva and towards Merdani and Dusina." Could you please draw that line, the Lasva-Merdani-Dusina line.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put number 2 somewhere in the middle of that line.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This will indicate to us that this is the axis indicated under item number 1 of this order. I would also kindly ask you to show us the direction or axis indicated at the bottom of this item, where it says that "the unit will follow the Lasva junction, Stara Pruga, Crna, TT852." Can you find all that, please? Yes, this is the local commune of Lasva. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here the Lasva junction, Stara Pruga Crna. This is a more wider section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Start with the Lasva junction, go to Stara Pruga, the old railway, and then go to TT Crna.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the railroad, the old railroad which went along the Lasva River?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But of course. There is no other old railroad, there is just the new one toward Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The old railroad follows the right bank of Lasva in this area. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then on towards the Crna trig point. What is here requested from the unit? How should it get to this line of defence? Did the commander order to do it in combat, or were they supposed to get that line in some other way?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that the unit should reach the defence line without combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark this axis by number 3, and this axis is the one that follows the route from the Lasva junction along the old railway to the Crna trig point.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document, and for that document we will have to go back to the previous map; the document is number 12, the exhibit number is P129. It describes the deployment of a mortar battery in the centre of Janjici village. Can you please mark the village of Janjici on this map.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mark it by the following number. Our previous number was 9, and the next one is 10.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now in relation to Dusina village, where is this village of Janjici? Is it on the same bank of the Lasva and Bosna rivers, or is it somewhere else, on another axis?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is on the same bank of the Bosna River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same bank of the Bosna River. And is it north or south from the village of Dusina?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is north-east from the village of Dusina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you please sign this map as well, the second map with all these different axes of movement. Can you please put your name, date, and sign the map.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, while the witness is doing that, I don't know if the Defence is planning on tendering these, but it might be helpful if they were to be given numbers now, rather than later, simply because we did switch back and forth between the two maps. And it just might make matters clearer if they were given numbers at this point rather than sometime later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I believe that it would be best. There are two maps; one is 1:50.000, the other is 1:100.000. And the 1:50.000 is 74. Can you please give us a number for this, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map will be admitted as DH1980; this is 1:50.000. And the map, the scale of which is 1:100.000, will be admitted as DH1980, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, there is a problem. You've given us the same number for two maps. Since the Chamber notices everything, I've noticed that as well. Can you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first map will be admitted as 1980; this is 1:50.000. And the second one will be 1981. There you go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. The Defence may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, we have now seen the orders given by the commander and the positions intended to defend the Lasva junction. Tell me, please, did the information that you receive regarding combat operations from your subordinate commands and units indicate to you at that time that there had been fighting in that area that went beyond the commander's orders; in other words, that lines should have been taken in the areas indicated by the orders, without any combat?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, without combat. However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection; those were leading questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence, please rephrase your question so that it is not leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, my first question would be as follows: Based on the documents that you have just seen, which were combat reports for that day, did you realise that there were combat activities in the area of Dusina?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did understand that from the reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reports themselves, did they give you -- provide you with an answer as to under which circumstances and how these combat operations take place?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not pay any attention to that; however, I believe that there were combat operations there. I don't know anything about the circumstances of those combat operations. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The previous orders that we have just seen, did they indicate that these units were engaged in combat in those areas where they were ordered to be deployed?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the orders that I've seen here, it says clearly that the positions should be taken without any fighting or combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do the orders sometimes envisage a situation where units may be engaged and are allowed to be engaged in combat; for example, as a situation when the unit has to defend itself?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basic military rule in any military force in the world, which includes the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, says that in case of attack while units are being deployed, the necessary resistance should be put up. It is possible that when the units are being transported and deployed, a sabotage unit of the enemy may be infiltrated, and that's why all the armies in the world say that if fire is opened, the unit should respond with fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will allow myself to say something at this point. General, I have followed what you have just told us, and I would like you to tell me, following what you have just said, in document P129, in paragraph 1, it is indicated at the end of this paragraph, in the English translation, "readiness for action." How do you explain "action" at 4.00 in the morning? What kind of action is this in military terms? When an order says "action," how would you interpret this word "action"? What is it? The date on the order is 25 January 1993, and the reference is made to an action which is supposed to take place at 4.00 in the morning on the 26th of January. So how do you interpret that phrase?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a customary military procedure, not only in the BiH army but in the armies of other countries, for an order to be issued on the 25th of January, and further on it is said that the march should take place during the night between the 25th and the 26th so that the position could be taken on the following day at 0400 hours. And this phrase, "combat readiness" at 4.00 on 26 January, says that the units should be prepared for action. Not to act, not to engage in combat, but should be ready to be engaged at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that this phrase should be read as follows: "The unit has to be ready to be engaged at 4.00," but it doesn't mean that it should be engaged in combat at that time. Thank you for your clarification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, this is precisely the way it should be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, one more question following on the Honourable Judge's question. Under item 1 the tasks are referred to. In order for a unit to be ready for combat, as you say, is it ordinary to carry out some tasks prior to that and to get to the final point specified in this order?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The unit has to be ready to carry out the tasks as indicated here. It has to get ready to carry out the task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, it has to carry out all the tasks specified under item 1 so as for its combat readiness is to be absolute if it is indeed to be engaged in combat, if that is ordered.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is precisely the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, I believe that I should ask one more question that I did not understand as somebody who is not very well-versed in the military, so I would like to continue with the General on that topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, on the following day, did you go back to the meeting of the Busovaca commission?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the following day, which was the 27th of January, I went back to Kiseljak, to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw the combat reports, and having been aware of Colonel Blaskic raising the issue, did General Hadzihasanovic take this issue seriously? And according to your information, did he issue an order for all the information that had reached you to be verified?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the first time that we officially received information that possibly an army unit had committed a war crime, which meant that the command should have checked all the details in order to verify whether there was, indeed, a crime committed in Dusina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would it be among the members of the corps command who should have investigated all the facts? Did your military police have all the capabilities at that moment to carry out that task on its own?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection; leading. That's a leading question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You came to the military police directly. Maybe you should have taken it a different way. So can you please rephrase your question. Rephrase, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The military police of the 3rd Corps, in January 1993, was it capable of performing all the tasks of the military police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the same thing. You should have asked him, but maybe I can do that. General, the Defence has asked you a question. If a crime was committed, who was in charge of doing investigations? Can you answer that, of course, as much as you were aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the crime was committed by a member of the military organisation, of the military, then it was the task of the military police to take the initial steps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. It has been asked and answered. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the commander task the military police to perform the part of their job that would result in the checking of this information?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He wanted a detailed investigation, as I've already said. The initial activities should have been carried out by the military police of the 3rd Corps, and the military police of the 3rd Corps did start doing that. However, they did not have enough personnel or equipment to do a high-quality investigation which would lead to a positive conclusion as to whether the casualties happened during combat or whether a crime had been committed. At that time the military police was not capable of doing that; they did not have any capabilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do you know if anybody else performed the verification of the facts? Did anybody else carry out the investigation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether, on that day, there was anybody else who performed those tasks. On that day, I left for Kiseljak; that was on the 27th. And when I returned, I received information that the civilian police would help with that, in other words, professionals from the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, at the meeting which you had in Busovaca, did you provide the attendants with the information that you had at your disposal? And was the cease-fire agreement signed on that day?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the reports that had reached us from the field, I received information that there had been combat operations in Dusina, and that there had been casualties on both sides during combat, on the side of the HVO and on the side of the BiH army. And this is the information that I have provided the attendants of the meeting with on the following day, on the 27th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Maybe we should stop here. I have endeavoured to finish the topic of Dusina, but I haven't been able to. I will continue on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, there have been a lot of changes. Could you please tell us exactly when is your next sitting? The register is going to tell me -- he has just told me that it will be on Thursday morning. General, as I have already told you, there is no sitting tomorrow. You may take a rest, because you have to come back on Thursday morning. As I have already indicated to you, you are not entitled to meet with anybody either from the Prosecution, from the Defence, or from the Bench. We shall see you on Thursday, at 9.00. And I will see everybody else on Thursday, at 9.00. Until then, I thank you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of December, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
